story.title: Noah and the Ark
story.subtitle: A promise after the storm

introduction.summary: In a violent and corrupt generation, Noah trusts God, builds the ark and becomes part of a new beginning marked by God’s covenant promise.
introduction.context: Human rebellion had spread throughout society. The flood narrative holds together the seriousness of evil, the obedience of Noah, God’s rescue and his commitment to preserve life.

storySections.title: A Corrupted World
storySections.content: Human violence and corruption fill the earth, bringing grief to God. Noah, however, is described as a righteous man who walks faithfully with God amid his generation.

storySections.title: Build the Ark
storySections.content: God warns Noah about the coming flood and gives detailed instructions for a vast ark. Noah is told to bring his household, provisions and representatives of the animal world. He responds by doing what God commands.

storySections.title: The Waters Rise
storySections.content: Noah’s family and the animals enter the ark. Rain falls and the floodwaters rise over the land. The ark carries its passengers safely through a crisis they could not survive on their own.

storySections.title: God Remembers Noah
storySections.content: The waters begin to recede. Noah sends out birds to discover whether the ground is dry. A dove eventually returns with a fresh olive leaf, signalling that new life is appearing again.

storySections.title: Covenant and Rainbow
storySections.content: Noah leaves the ark and worships God. God establishes a covenant with Noah, his descendants and every living creature. The rainbow becomes the sign of God’s promise that a flood will never again destroy all life on earth.

keyPeople.name: Noah’s family

flashcards.front: Why did God instruct Noah to build an ark?
flashcards.back: A flood was coming in response to widespread corruption, and the ark would preserve Noah’s household and animal life.

flashcards.front: How did Noah respond to God’s instructions?
flashcards.back: Noah did everything God commanded him to do.

flashcards.front: How long did the rain fall?
flashcards.back: The rain fell for forty days and forty nights.

flashcards.front: What sign showed Noah that vegetation was returning?
flashcards.back: A dove returned carrying a freshly plucked olive leaf.

flashcards.front: What was Noah’s first recorded act after leaving the ark?
flashcards.back: Noah built an altar and worshipped God.
It was the sign of God’s covenant with the earth and every living creature.

keyLessons: Faithful obedience matters even when God’s instruction is difficult.
God takes violence and corruption seriously.
God provides rescue and remembers those who trust him.
The rainbow points to God’s covenant mercy and commitment to life.

reflection.question: What act of obedience might require you to trust God before you can see the outcome?
reflection.prompt: Write down one clear next step and decide when you will take it.

story.prayerPrompt: Faithful God, give me courage to obey you and remember your promises when the way ahead is uncertain.

quiz.question: How is Noah described in his generation?
options: A righteous man who walked with God
quiz.explanation: Noah stood apart from the corruption around him by walking faithfully with God.

quiz.question: What material was Noah told to use for the ark?
quiz.explanation: Genesis records God instructing Noah to make the ark from gopher wood.

quiz.question: What did the dove bring back?
quiz.explanation: The fresh olive leaf showed that the floodwater had receded from the earth.

quiz.question: Where did the ark come to rest?
quiz.explanation: The ark rested in the region called the mountains of Ararat.

quiz.question: What sign accompanied God’s covenant?
quiz.explanation: God appointed the rainbow as the visible sign of his covenant with living creatures.
